repo_rows.name: audio-extract-mix
repo_rows.description: Use when you need to EXTRACT, MIX, REPLACE, DUCK, or LOUDNESS-NORMALIZE audio on a video/clip with ffmpeg — e.g. pull a wav out of a clip, lay a music bed or VO UNDER a speaker so it auto-dips when they talk (sidechain ducking), normalize an export to a per-platform LUFS target (-14 for TikTok/Reels/Shorts/YouTube, -23 EBU R128 broadcast, -24 ATSC), mux/replace/strip an audio track while preserving all other streams, or turn the soundtrack into laughter/applause/ music/loudness saliency signals. The exact filter graphs, argv lists, codec/map choices, and the pitfalls that actually bite (amix auto-attenuation, -shortest duration, stream-index = list-order coupling, mono/32k decode for PANNs, loudnorm single-pass drift) come from the real media_studio source cited below. Do NOT use for: per-word transcription/alignment (use ASR/CTC modules), TTS dub GENERATION (this only muxes a finished dub), pitch/tempo time-stretch, or pure visual edits. Do NOT use as a generic "run ffmpeg" reference — it is scoped to these audio ops with the project's frozen wire surface.

BC is a CUSTOM PONOS C++/GLES engine (not cocos2d-x). Use to script/inspect BC menus or read scene state.

repo_rows.name: bc-drive-plus

repo_rows.name: bc-update-survival
repo_rows.description: Use when a Battle Cats (EN, jp.co.ponos.battlecatsen) update relinks lib/x86_64/libnative-lib.so and your pinned RVAs go stale — the toolpack that RETIRES hardcoded offsets. AOB wildcard-signature resolver (author a byte pattern that wildcards only the reloc-sensitive bytes, then re-locate the function by pattern via offline .so scan or live `frida search_memory`/Memory.scan — survives relink where a fixed RVA does not); ghidriff one-command cross-version .so diff that AUTO-PORTS the whole offset table old→new; and a per-version-bump update-triage (extract + sha-compare + diff APK/DAT/.so). Ships a SHADOW-mode drift gate (observe + log only, never blocks). Use before trusting any bc-drive / battlecats-event-unlock offset after a version bump. NOT for save-file edits (bcsfe-save-roundtrip) or live UI driving (bc-drive).

repo_rows.name: execution-grounded-bon

repo_rows.name: ida-multi-mcp

repo_rows.name: silence-trim
repo_rows.description: Use when removing long silences / dead air / filler-pauses from a TALKING video to produce a tight, jump-cut style edit (podcast, vlog, lecture, screen recording, talking-head short). Detects silent spans with ffmpeg `silencedetect` (noise floor in dB + a minimum silence duration), inverts them to KEEP spans leaving a small pad on each edge so cuts don't sound clipped, then re-cuts frame-accurately with a `trim`/`atrim` + `concat` filter_complex — and re-times caption cues onto the compacted timeline so subtitles don't drift late after every removed gap. Do NOT use for: removing background noise while keeping length (that's denoise/filtering, not trimming); music tracks or ambient/B-roll with no speech (everything reads as "silence" and you gut the clip — or as "loud" and nothing cuts); VAD-grade speech/non-speech where the noise floor is high (silencedetect is amplitude-only, not a voice classifier); or audio-event scoring (laughter/applause salience — that's the PANNs audio_saliency path, a different module). Source of truth: sidecar/media_studio/features/silencetrim.py.

Ships as a SHADOW-mode advisory oracle (observe + log to a bounded rotating sink, never blocks CI or nags). repo_rows.name: workflow-foundry
repo_rows.description: Use when RUNNING a multi-agent fan-out on this estate — dispatching N parallel work units, deciding barrier-vs-pipeline, gating fan-in, or judging whether a unit is actually done. The operating contract distilled from measured runs here, not generic advice: freeze the SHA and the spawn preamble before the first unit launches; fan in on RECEIPTS (Test-Path every contracted output BEFORE reading any digest — 3/3 agents once returned plausible digests for files that did not exist); UNIT-COMPLETE is a string the unit writes about itself, not proof; pipeline by default and use a barrier only when stage N genuinely needs ALL of stage N-1; write-as-you-go (a 70-minute unit produced 691 KB and wrote nothing, unrecoverable); both-states controls (a probe silent in the broken state measures nothing); never fan a MECHANICAL comparison out to LLM judgement (measured 86% accuracy with 100% of errors in the dangerous direction against an exact 40-line differ); per-needle deferral is the wrong LAYER and recurses, only a role-aware discriminator terminates; adversarial verifiers get siblings FULL text not digests; and most refutations are OVERCLAIMS where the code was right and the sentence was too wide — fix the sentence. Ships a runnable receipt gate with a built-in both-states self-test. Triggers include fan out N agents, gate the fan-in, is this unit done, my parallel phase deadlocked, an agent returned a digest for a missing file, design the work-unit decomposition, review the siblings adversarially. NOT for writing the workflow .mjs runtime code (use workflow-authoring), NOT for the cross-vendor Codex dispatch transport (use cross-vendor-dispatch and multi-ai-mingle), NOT for remote compute placement (use codex-databricks-fanout).

Ships a runnable receipt gate with a built-in both-states self-test. Triggers include fan out N agents, gate the fan-in, is this unit done, my parallel phase deadlocked, an agent returned a digest for a missing file, design the work-unit decomposition, review the siblings adversarially. NOT for writing the workflow .mjs runtime code (use workflow-authoring), NOT for the cross-vendor Codex dispatch transport (use cross-vendor-dispatch and multi-ai-mingle), NOT for remote compute placement (use codex-databricks-fanout).

live_rows.name: silence-trim
live_rows.description: Use when removing long silences / dead air / filler-pauses from a TALKING video to produce a tight, jump-cut style edit (podcast, vlog, lecture, screen recording, talking-head short). Detects silent spans with ffmpeg `silencedetect` (noise floor in dB + a minimum silence duration), inverts them to KEEP spans leaving a small pad on each edge so cuts don't sound clipped, then re-cuts frame-accurately with a `trim`/`atrim` + `concat` filter_complex — and re-times caption cues onto the compacted timeline so subtitles don't drift late after every removed gap. Do NOT use for: removing background noise while keeping length (that's denoise/filtering, not trimming); music tracks or ambient/B-roll with no speech (everything reads as "silence" and you gut the clip — or as "loud" and nothing cuts); VAD-grade speech/non-speech where the noise floor is high (silencedetect is amplitude-only, not a voice classifier); or audio-event scoring (laughter/applause salience — that's the PANNs audio_saliency path, a different module). Source of truth: sidecar/media_studio/features/silencetrim.py.

Model-based testing via fast-check (`fc.commands` + `fc.asyncModelRun`) driving Playwright, with automatic shrinking to a minimal reproducing click/nav sequence. Ships as a SHADOW-mode advisory oracle (observe + log to a bounded rotating sink, never blocks CI or nags). Optionally deepen the existing Python Hypothesis suite with HypoFuzz nightly — but ONLY after verifying HypoFuzz's shifted license; the fast-check oracle ships regardless. NOT for pixel/design critique (use ui-audit), NOT for deterministic single-flow E2E (use Playwright directly).

live_rows.name: video-stabilize
live_rows.description: Use when stabilizing a shaky / handheld / camera-shake video so it looks steadied (locked-down or smooth-pan). live_rows.name: video-watermark-removal

PRIMARY method = ProPainter flow-guided temporal inpaint on a TIGHT logo-only mask (pulls REAL background pixels from neighbouring frames -> sharp, no soft haze), CHUNKED in time to fit a small GPU, with PER-FRAME presence gating so occluded frames stay pristine. big-LAMA is the fast SOFT fallback.

live_rows.name: workflow-authoring
live_rows.description: Use when writing or debugging a saved Claude Code Workflow (a .js/.mjs script under ~/.claude/workflows using the injected agent/parallel/phase globals to fan out subagents). Covers the runtime API, banned Date.now() non-determinism, worktree isolation, per-fan-in schemas, null-tolerant barriers, and the typed Codex output-schema landmine. Triggers: author a workflow, fan out subagents.

live_rows.name: workflow-foundry
live_rows.description: Use when RUNNING a multi-agent fan-out on this estate — dispatching N parallel work units, deciding barrier-vs-pipeline, gating fan-in, or judging whether a unit is actually done. The operating contract distilled from measured runs here, not generic advice: freeze the SHA and the spawn preamble before the first unit launches; fan in on RECEIPTS (Test-Path every contracted output BEFORE reading any digest — 3/3 agents once returned plausible digests for files that did not exist); UNIT-COMPLETE is a string the unit writes about itself, not proof; pipeline by default and use a barrier only when stage N genuinely needs ALL of stage N-1; write-as-you-go (a 70-minute unit produced 691 KB and wrote nothing, unrecoverable); both-states controls (a probe silent in the broken state measures nothing); never fan a MECHANICAL comparison out to LLM judgement (measured 86% accuracy with 100% of errors in the dangerous direction against an exact 40-line differ); per-needle deferral is the wrong LAYER and recurses, only a role-aware discriminator terminates; adversarial verifiers get siblings FULL text not digests; and most refutations are OVERCLAIMS where the code was right and the sentence was too wide — fix the sentence. Ships a runnable receipt gate with a built-in both-states self-test. Triggers include fan out N agents, gate the fan-in, is this unit done, my parallel phase deadlocked, an agent returned a digest for a missing file, design the work-unit decomposition, review the siblings adversarially. NOT for writing the workflow .mjs runtime code (use workflow-authoring), NOT for the cross-vendor Codex dispatch transport (use cross-vendor-dispatch and multi-ai-mingle), NOT for remote compute placement (use codex-databricks-fanout).

live_rows.name: workflow-monitor
live_rows.description: Use when you want to LIVE-monitor a Claude Code Workflow ("ultracode") fan-out — watch every parallel agent's status, lens/task, model, tokens, tool activity, and final result across the WHOLE FLEET (all sessions/projects) in a read-only terminal cockpit, instead of the sparse native /workflows view or opening a terminal-tail per agent. Also for triaging errored/retrying/stalled agents mid-run, or reviewing a finished run's per-agent prompt/output.
